p: yourselves: That which he mentioned before briefly concerning his apostleship, he handles now more at large, and to that end and purpose which we spoke of.
But even after that we had: The virtues of a true pastor are freely without fear to preach the Gospel, even in the midst of dangers.
our God to speak unto you: Through God's gracious help.
For our exhortation was not of: To teach pure doctrine faithfully and with a pure heart.
uncleanness: By any wicked and evil type of dealing.
But as we were: To approve his conscience to God, being free from all flattery and covetousness.

allowed of God to be put: There is this difference between the judgments of God and the judgments of men, that when men choose, they give regard to the qualities of those things which stand before them, but God finds the reason of his counsel only in himself. Therefore, it follows that seeing as we are not able to think a good thought, that whoever he first chooses to those callings, he does not find them able but indeed makes them able. And therefore in that we are empowered of God, it depends upon his mercy.
trieth our hearts: Who approves and allows them.
Nor of men sought we glory: To submit himself even to the basest, to win them, and to avoid all pride.
burdensome: When I might lawfully have lived upon the expenses of the churches.
gentle among you: We were rough, and yet easy and gentle as a nurse that is neither seeking glory, nor covetous, but who takes all pains as patiently as if she were a mother.
So being affectionately desirous of you: To consider the flock that is committed to him as more important than his own life.
For ye remember: To let go of his own rights, rather than to be a cost to his sheep.
Ye are witnesses: To excel others in the example of a godly life.
As ye know how we exhorted: To exhort and comfort with a fatherly mind and affection.
That ye would walk worthy of: To exhort all men diligently and earnestly to lead a godly life.

For this cause also thank we: Having approved his ministry, he commends again (to that end and purpose that I spoke of) the cheerfulness of the Thessalonians which was due to his diligence in preaching, and their brave patience.

For ye: He strengthens and encourages them in their afflictions which they suffered among their own people, because they were afflicted by their own countrymen. And this happened, he says, to the churches of the Jews, as well as to them: and therefore they ought to take it in good part.
Christ Jesus: Which Christ has gathered together.
countrymen: Even from those who are from the same country and the same town that you are from.

Who both killed the Lord Jesus: He prevents an offence which might be taken, because the Jews especially above all others persecuted the Gospel. That is no new thing, he says, seeing that they slew Christ himself, and his Prophets, and have banished me also.
and they please not God: He foretells the utter destruction of the Jews, lest any man should be moved by their rebellion.
all men: For the Jews would neither enter into the kingdom of God themselves, nor allow others to enter in.

fill up their sins alway: Until that wickedness of theirs which they have by inheritance as it were of their fathers, has grown so great, that the measure of their iniquity being filled, God may come forth to wrath.

wrath is come upon them to: The judgment of God who was angry, which indeed appeared shortly after in the destruction of the city of Jerusalem, where many fled even out of various provinces, when it was besieged.

But we: He meets with an objection, why he did not come to them immediately, being in such great misery: I often desired to, he says, and I was not able, but Satan hindered my endeavours, and therefore I sent Timothy my faithful companion to you, because you are most dear to me.
being taken from you for a: Were kept apart from you, and as it were orphans.
